bridge_reviews.comment: The norm definition, non-zero normalization rule, zero-vector safeguard, worked example, RC-item bindings, and scope are correct and pedagogically sufficient. Replace or supplement SRC-01 with a direct institutional source location that explicitly states the Euclidean-norm formula and supports normalization of a non-zero vector. The current MIT URL and locator identify only table-of-contents headings, so they do not provide auditable evidence for BC-01 through BC-04.

The orthogonality and orthonormality statements and scalar coefficient v^T x are correct and support RC-003, RC-006, RC-007, and RC-012. Revise SRC-01 and SRC-02 to bind BC-01 through BC-04 to direct lecture-summary or transcript locations containing the relevant definitions and coefficient formula rather than to overview pages. Also narrow BC-03 and BC-04 to the scalar coefficient v^T x: remove the additional vector-projection formula (v^T x)v and projected vector (3, 0)^T, because the Frozen Curriculum Model boundary authorizes the scalar projection coefficient needed by the Contract and explicitly reserves the later spectral/eigenbasis content.

The inner-product definition, x^T x identity, x^T A x procedure, numerical example, exclusions, and RC-009/RC-010 support are correct and remain within the prerequisite boundary. SRC-02 directly supports computing x^T A x, but SRC-01 is only a table-of-contents page. Replace or supplement SRC-01 with a direct institutional passage that explicitly supports x^T y as a dot product and x^T x = ||x||_2^2, then update the evidence locator and content bindings.

Approved. The array conversion, shape inspection, matrix-vector multiplication, default one-dimensional Euclidean norm, scalar zero check, explicit exception pattern, elementwise-comparison warning, and tuple return/unpacking pattern are correct. The official NumPy and Python documentation directly supports the five content blocks, the content remains limited to operations required by RC-016, RC-017, and RC-018, and no alternative solver or Contract-algorithm change is introduced.

overall_review.comment: The four-bridge demand set and all RC/profile bindings are correct. The NumPy bridge is approved. The three mathematical bridges are mathematically correct and pedagogically sufficient, but their source evidence must be made directly auditable; the orthogonality/projection bridge must additionally be narrowed to scalar projection coefficients. Rebuild the candidate in a new directory with only these source-binding and boundary changes, rerun the same bridge validator, and generate a fresh fully pending review.
